Video QC: annotation audit and blind Astra evaluation

27 October 2026 · audit complete; blind evaluation in progress

I would not promote another defect into the current 48-item ground truth on the evidence reviewed so far. Most apparent additions are already covered by existing labels, or are not sufficiently distinguishable from rotation, occlusion or deliberate performance. This is a sampled visual audit, not an exhaustive claim that the videos contain no other defects.

No Astra score yet. The independent blind v2 batch is running. Scores will be calculated only after predictions are frozen. Existing ground truth, adjudications and the public leaderboard remain unchanged.

The answer key has advanced beyond the original human-review file

The original Markdown review lists 36 defects; the structured truth now contains 48 defects worth 141 points. The extra 12 include model-prompted, human-confirmed observations. Examples include the double tie and extra-finger annotation in man-cups, duplicate reflected door in dancer-mirror, meal chronology in the diner, and the audio claim in dialogue. Those are not new discoveries from this run.

Dialogue remains a visual false-positive control, but it is not an audio-clean clip under the current truth: DIAL-1 is worth two points. This audit has not independently listened to that audio.

Evidence and rejected additions

Why I did not add a new block-digit defect

The rightmost block changes from showing 3 to showing 6 near 7.75s. Its orientation also changes, and a 3 is visible on its side afterward. A digit-only claim has not ruled out rotation. The multiplication and color transformations remain covered by BLOC-1.

Why I did not add receiving-jar hardware or vanishing tweezers

Scoring issues to resolve separately from this run

  1. Clarify ambiguous labels. OLIV-1 explicitly permits dark olives being hidden below green ones. LONG-5 says the man seems to bring his own cup, which alone is not a physical impossibility. Preserve their current scores here, but require timestamped evidence and an explicit reason these count as defects for future benchmark revisions.
  2. Make units of credit explicit. Several labels combine multiple observations: LONG-6 combines counter intersection and a missing woman; PHON-1 combines text corruption and unresponsive UI. The scorer currently maps each finding to one defect ID. Define which component suffices for a match, and how a single finding describing two separate defects is handled, before changing adjudication rules.
  3. Separate detection from reporting discipline. Detection counts each truth defect once; each false-positive finding costs one point, including repeated claims across samples. More sampling can increase recall and lower the final score simultaneously. Report both axes and the component runs.
  4. Do not treat corroboration as confirmation. Repeated model claims can share a bias. Any new candidate remains neutral pending evidence and human adjudication, rather than automatically receiving truth credit.
  5. Freeze priorities and denominators. DANC-4’s description still says its P3 priority awaits KT confirmation. The diner contributes 57/141 points (40.4%), so a few diner labels strongly affect rankings.

Blind v2 run: exact architecture and limits

GPT-6 Astra, high reasoning, default service tier. The six unchanged core roles run independently for each clip (84 evaluations). A separate perceptual inventory determines the routed checks; its decisions are frozen and reused across three independent samples. The resulting union receives unique defect credit and a one-point penalty per false-positive finding. No rejected global-confound prompt and no self-verification pass.

The evaluator received opaque video names, generic protocol prompts and a clean conversation, without the answer key or prior outputs. This is procedural blinding on a shared filesystem, not an OS-enforced security boundary. The existing v2 router was developed from this dataset and contains dataset-informed examples; therefore the evaluation is blind to the labels, but is not evidence of performance on an unseen holdout set.

Actual media input is extracted frames, with optional denser inspection. Native video/audio API entries have different input affordances. Audio is currently unassessed. Retain the official 141-point denominator and explicitly identify the missed/unassessed audio component; a supplemental visual-only denominator is 139. A full statistical claim about Astra’s run-to-run variance would require repeated complete runs, not merely the three routed samples.

Audit method: 2fps contact sheets for all 13 short clips; 4-second overview sampling of the long clip; original-resolution follow-ups and a 24fps local sequence where needed. No independent audio playback. Supporting frames, reference snapshots, delegation receipt and machine-readable audit are retained in RUNS/261027 GPT6 Astra blind audit/. The blind predictions have not been used to form this parent audit.
